text:
Elaine: heads up — I ran a small quantized benchmark with the new kernel-selector heuristics and saw weird tail latency variance under a power cap. attaching notes.
Jorge: thanks — what GPU and power cap? did you pin clocks?
Elaine: A100-sxm, power capped to 120W via nvidia-smi -pl 120, mem/freq locked. runtime build: commit f2a9c3, int8+fp8 kernels enabled.
Samir: rough numbers? p50/p95? batch sizes? seq len?
Elaine: baseline fp16 p50=9.8ms p95=25.7ms tokens/s=2100 (bs=8, seq=1024 warmup=50 iters). int8 calibrated p50=10.2ms p95=31.4ms tokens/s=1950. but with kernel-selector auto we saw 14% p95 regression on mixed batches (variable seq lengths).
Jorge: mixed batches meaning batching heuristic grouped different seq lengths together and kernel chooser picked the slow path more frequently?
Elaine: yes — kernel-selector preferred int8_kern_v2 for long seqs but fell back to scalar_fp8 for certain kv-cache sizes; fallback happened ~18% of requests during steady state.
Kai: do we track KV cache hit/eviction metrics? fallback should correlate with KV reallocs.
Elaine: perf-bot attached logs: "kv_cache_reallocs=23 per_min, kv_evictions=7, avg_kv_pages=1.8" — eviction spikes aligned with p95 spikes.
PerfBot: AUTOMATED: warmup completed (50 iters). profile summary attached: avg_kernel_time_int8=0.42ms, avg_kernel_time_fp16=0.36ms, kernel_switch_count=124
Maria: possible causes: calibration quant ranges causing different kernel paths? or allocator fragmentation under power limit.
Samir: also tokenization. were the inputs tokenized the same between runs? different chunking can change kv lengths.
Elaine: yes, used HF tokenizer v0.15.1 with same seed. I used mixed prompt lengths (50% short, 50% long) to simulate production. I can re-run with homogeneous inputs.
Jorge: for fair comparison we should fix: 1) same tokenizer+vocab; 2) same warmup (both power and model warmup) — recommend 200 warmup iterations for quantized runs; 3) stable power & clocks; 4) single-run golden harness to capture p50/p95/p99; 5) record kernel decisions and KV alloc traces.
Kai: +1 to recording kernel decisions. can we add a histogram of kernel durations and a per-kernel callcount? That helps spot hot fallbacks.
Elaine: I pushed a tiny patch to the perf tracer: perf-trace --dump-kernel-hist --dump-kv-events. example output snippet:
```
kernel:int8_kern_v2 calls=812 mean=0.41ms p95=0.98ms
kernel:scalar_fp8 calls=152 mean=0.88ms p95=1.9ms
kv_event:realloc at 00:12:34 size=64 pages
```
Maria: Nice. Also we need to control for temperature: under 120W the GPU thermals hit higher temps and throttle may vary across runs. log temps and use the same ambient for each comparison.
Samir: for calibration-induced perf differences—are we reusing calibration tables across runs? calibration can change activation ranges and the quant kernels might choose different slow paths.
Elaine: I ran two calib strategies: per-layer static (calibA) and dynamic range clip (calibB). calibA produced slightly better quality but triggered more per-op guards -> slower. calibB had smaller quant ranges -> fewer guards but slightly worse logprob.
Jorge: we should include quality metrics in the benchmark: perplexity on a holdout prompt set and a few probe prompts (summaries) and use rouge/bert-score for regression detection.
Kai: agree. Also measure tokens/s while excluding prompt tokenization time vs end-to-end latency. Two measurement modes: tokenized-run (runtime receives tokens) and raw-text-run (we include tokenizer). Both matter for different customers.
Elaine: proposal for benchmark methodology (short):
- Setup: lock power & clocks, stable temp, same CUDA/cudnn/drivers, HF tokenizer pinned
- Warmup: 200 iterations for quantized kernels (both KV priming & kernel code paths)
- Input distribution: run two suites: homogeneous seq lengths (64/256/1024) and mixed realistic distribution
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, kernel histograms, kv_event logs, gpu power/temps, kernel_switch counts
- Calibration: run both calib strategies and include quality delta (perp + probe metrics)
- Repeat: 5 runs per config, report median of medians and stddev
- Golden run: an isolated single-run with verbose tracing to capture exact kernel decisions
Samir: sounds solid. add a note to use identical batching heuristic config. we should freeze the heuristic parameters (min_batch_timeout, max_batch_tokens) across comparisons.
Maria: and record seed + git sha + docker image + dataset digest in each run metadata.
Elaine: yes. I saved a sample run command:
```
./bench_runner --model /models/galaxy-7b-quant --batcher-config=prod-frozen.json \n  --warmup-iters=200 --power-limit=120 --tokenized-inputs --trace-dir=out/1965123456
nvidia-smi -i 0 --query-gpu=power.limit,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 > out/gpu_stats.csv &
```
Jorge: good. next steps: Elaine re-run homogeneous suite and attach per-kernel histograms + kv traces. Samir will try to reproduce on a V100 (different architecture). Kai will wire the perf-tracer hist summary to the benchmark dashboard.
Elaine: re-running now, will post a compact summary when done. if anyone has objections to the methodology, speak now. otherwise I'll convert this into a runbook doc.
Maria: no objections. please include a short checklist for fairness: same tokenizer, identical batching params, locked power/clocks, same warmup count, same input distribution.
Samir: one more: when comparing int8 vs fp16, make sure to match quality thresholds — a faster int8 is useless if logprob delta > 0.5 on the probe set. include delta thresholds.
Elaine: noted. thanks all :thumbsup!
PerfBot: NOTE: scheduled golden-run harness at 2026-09-20T03:00Z.
